name: Seasonal Influenza (Flu A & B)
shortDesc: Systemic viral infection characterized by sudden high fever, body aches, and respiratory fatigue.
fullDesc: Influenza viruses infect the epithelial cells of the respiratory tract. Transmission occurs via aerosol droplets. Rapid onset requires immediate rest and early therapeutic intervention.
protocols: Optimal bed rest during peak febrile periods (days 1 through 4)
Oral rehydration solution containing balanced sodium and glucose
Antipyretics used according to clinical guidelines for fever comfort
Targeted antiviral therapies evaluated by healthcare professionals within 48 hours
timeline: 7 to 10 days for full acute symptom resolution. Persistent fatigue may continue for two weeks.

name: Acute Rhinovirus Cold
shortDesc: Mild upper respiratory viral illness centered primarily in nasal passages and throat mucosa.
fullDesc: Rhinoviruses thrive in cooler nasal temperatures, causing localized swelling, sneezing, and clear mucosal secretions without severe systemic fever.
protocols: Saline nasal rinses to clear congested airways gently
Warm fluid consumption including honey infusions for sore throat ease
Adequate sleep to facilitate endogenous immune antibody production
Humidified air exposure to soothe inflamed upper airway passages
timeline: 5 to 7 days. Most individuals return to baseline activities within one week.

name: Systemic Viral Fever Syndrome
shortDesc: Fever response accompanying non specific viral exposure, often causing chills and weakness.
fullDesc: Systemic immune signaling releases cytokines, triggering hypothalamic thermoregulation shifts that elevate body temperature to combat viral replication.
protocols: Frequent core temperature monitoring every four hours
Light breathable clothing and cool ambient room environments
Continuous fluid intake to replenish perspiration losses
Avoidance of heavy physical strain until fever subsides completely
timeline: 3 to 5 days of febrile activity followed by gradual energy recovery.

name: Acute Viral Bronchitis
shortDesc: Inflammation of bronchial air passages following initial viral colds or flu infections.
fullDesc: Viral inflammation increases bronchial mucus production, leading to persistent coughing fits aimed at clearing bronchial passages.
protocols: Steam inhalation treatments twice daily for bronchial relaxation
Cough suppressant or expectorant formulations as guided by physicians
Complete avoidance of environmental smoke or chemical irritants
High volume fluid intake to thin bronchial secretions effectively
timeline: 10 to 21 days for bronchial cough clearance.
